account-refusal-unavailable.string: The user accounts of this system could not be read.

account-refusal-unknown-group.string: One of the groups does not exist, or is about to be removed.

account-refusal-root.string: {name} is a root account. Garuda Toolbox does not change it.

account-refusal-current-user.string: {name} is the account you are logged in with. It cannot lock or remove itself.

account-refusal-system-account.string: {name} is a system account. Only accounts of people can be removed.

account-refusal-outside-user-range.string: {name} has a user ID outside 1000 to 60000, so it stays as it is.

account-refusal-last-admin.string: {name} is the last member of the groups wheel and sudo. Without one nobody could administer this system.

account-refusal-last-admin-lock.string: {name} is the last member of the groups wheel and sudo. With a locked password nobody could administer this system.

account-refusal-lock-state-unknown.string: {name} cannot be locked while it is unknown which admins are locked.

account-refusal-primary-group.string: {name} is the primary group of a user, so it stays.

account-refusal-system-group.string: {name} is a system group. Installed programs rely on it.

account-refusal-shell-not-listed.string: This shell is not listed in /etc/shells.

account-refusal-uid-in-use.string: Another account already has this user ID.

account-refusal-uid-out-of-range.string: Accounts of people take a user ID from 1000 to 60000, system accounts one below 1000.

account-refusal-home-taken.string: Another account already has this home folder.

page-boot-subtitle.string: Applying the changes writes /etc/default/grub, keeps the old file as a backup and builds the boot menu again.

page-boot-subtitle-sdboot.string: The settings of systemd-boot and the kernel command line that is built into each kernel image.

boot-failed.string: The GRUB settings could not be read

boot-failed-detail.string: The note at the bottom of the window says why. Read again tries once more.

boot-missing.string: GRUB is not the boot loader of this system

boot-missing-detail.string: There is no /etc/default/grub, so this page has nothing to change. Other boot loaders are configured with their own tools.

boot-vm.string: You are running in a virtual machine. The boot splash works there in a limited way.

boot-refused-unavailable.string: This system has no /etc/default/grub, so there is nothing to change.
boot-refused-unavailable.developer_comment: Why an edit was not queued.

boot-refused-custom-command-line.string: The kernel command line is not changed here. Edit /etc/default/grub on the Config Files page.

boot-refused-too-many-parameters.string: The kernel command line is full.

boot-refused-unknown-theme.string: This is not an installed Plymouth theme: {value}

boot-refused-no-kernel-cmdline.string: This system has no /etc/kernel/cmdline. Its boot entries carry their own parameters, so there is nothing to change.

boot-refused-custom-kernel-cmdline.string: The kernel command line is not changed here. Edit /etc/kernel/cmdline on the Config Files page.

boot-refused-protected-parameter.string: {value} stays: without it the system finds no root file system to start.

boot-refused-invalid-character.string: This holds a character that is not allowed here, such as a blank, a quote, a backslash or a dollar sign: {value}

boot-refused-invalid-path.string: This is not a full path to a file: {value}

boot-refused-wrong-type.string: This is not a file of the right type: {value}

boot-default-known.string: The menu entry that is booted when you do not pick another.

boot-default-missing.string: GRUB has not generated a boot menu yet, so there are no entries to choose from.

boot-default-dismissed.string: The password dialog was closed, so the boot menu was not read and its entries are not listed. Read again tries once more.

boot-default-denied.string: The boot menu was not read: the password dialog was closed or the password was not accepted. Its entries are not listed. Read again tries once more.

boot-default-no-agent.string: The boot menu was not read, because no password dialog could appear: this desktop session runs no polkit authentication agent. Its entries are not listed.

boot-default-helper-missing.string: The boot menu was not read, because the helper of Garuda Toolbox is not installed. Its entries are not listed. Reinstall Garuda Toolbox.

boot-default-unknown.string: The boot menu could not be read, so its entries are not listed. Read again tries once more.

boot-default-not-asked.string: The boot menu has not been read yet. Read again reads it.

boot-default-remembered.string: GRUB boots the entry that was booted last.

boot-remember-detail.string: Makes the entry you booted last the default for the next start.

boot-timeout-detail.string: The seconds the menu waits before it boots the default entry.

boot-timeout-unknown.string: The file holds a timeout that is no number. Choosing one here replaces it.

boot-timeout-unit.developer_comment: The unit after the timeout's number, the symbol for seconds.

boot-submenus-detail.string: Off shows every entry in the top menu, without "Advanced options".

boot-os-prober-detail.string: Adds other installed systems to the boot menu with os-prober.

boot-proposal-offer.string: The menu entry of the kernel {kernel} can become the default. Nothing is queued until you choose Queue as default.
boot-proposal-offer.developer_comment: A kernel the Kernels page proposed as the default.

boot-proposal-same.string: The kernel {kernel} already is the default entry.

boot-proposal-remember.string: GRUB boots the entry that was booted last. Switch Remember the last entry off to make the kernel {kernel} the default.

boot-proposal-none.string: The boot menu has no entry for the kernel {kernel}. Pick the entry yourself, or generate the menu again by applying any change of this page.

boot-proposal-sdboot-none.string: systemd-boot has no image of the kernel {kernel} yet. Its image is built when the kernel is installed or updated. Pick the entry yourself once it is there.

boot-proposal-loading.string: Looking for the boot menu entry of the kernel {kernel}…

boot-parameters-detail.string: Each parameter is one word such as nowatchdog or loglevel=3. They are written to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT.

boot-parameters-custom.string: The kernel command line holds quotes or other characters this page does not change: {line} Edit /etc/default/grub on the Config Files page instead.

boot-parameter-kept.string: {parameter} stays: without it the system finds no root file system to start.

boot-flag-quiet-detail.string: Off shows every message of the kernel while the system starts.

boot-flag-splash-detail.string: Shows a graphical boot animation instead of text. It is drawn by Plymouth, which is queued for installation when it is missing.

boot-flag-mitigations-off-detail.string: Disables CPU security mitigations for better performance but less security.

boot-flag-sysrq-detail.string: Keeps the key combinations for emergency system control switched on.

boot-plymouth-detail.string: The animation Plymouth shows while the system starts. Applying it builds the initramfs again (the small start-up system the kernel loads first), which takes a while.

boot-plymouth-queued.string: Plymouth is queued for installation. Choose a theme after it is installed.

boot-plymouth-missing.string: Plymouth is not installed, so there are no themes to choose from.

boot-background-detail.string: A PNG, JPEG or TGA picture behind the boot menu. A GRUB theme has its own background.

boot-background-from-theme.string: Set in /etc/default/grub as GRUB_MENU_PICTURE, which some GRUB themes read. Choose a picture to replace it.

boot-theme-detail.string: The theme.txt file of a GRUB theme, usually below /usr/share/grub/themes.

boot-file-choose.developer_comment: $name is the field's name, such as GRUB theme.

boot-sdboot-unset.developer_comment: systemd-boot, shown instead of the GRUB settings.

boot-sdboot-default-first.string: The first entry of the menu

boot-sdboot-timeout-detail.string: How long the menu waits before it starts the default entry.

boot-sdboot-timeout-menu-force.string: The menu waits for a key

boot-sdboot-timeout-menu-hidden.string: Hidden unless a key is held at start

boot-sdboot-editor-detail.string: Lets anyone at the machine change the kernel command line in the menu.

boot-sdboot-auto-entries-detail.string: Other systems on the disk, such as Windows.

boot-sdboot-auto-firmware-detail.string: An entry that restarts into the firmware's setup.

boot-sdboot-parameters-detail.string: Each parameter is one word such as nowatchdog or loglevel=3. They are written to /etc/kernel/cmdline and built into each kernel image.

boot-sdboot-parameters-custom.string: The kernel command line holds quotes or other characters this page does not change: {line} Edit /etc/kernel/cmdline on the Config Files page instead.

boot-sdboot-cmdline-running.string: /etc/kernel/cmdline does not exist yet, so these are the parameters the system started with. The first change creates the file.

boot-sdboot-no-cmdline.string: This system has no /etc/kernel/cmdline. Its boot entries carry their own parameters.

page-boot-repair-subtitle.string: Install the boot loader of a system that does not start again, or build its boot files again.

repair-intro.string: Use this page when an installed system does not start anymore. It installs the boot loader of that system again, GRUB or systemd-boot, or builds its boot files again: GRUB's boot menu, or systemd-boot's kernel images.

repair-asks-first.string: Each repair asks first and names the partition and the disk it writes to. A GRUB system with /boot on a partition of its own, or with its EFI system partition somewhere else than /boot/efi, is not repaired here.

repair-test-mode.string: Test mode: this page is meant for the live system and shows here only because Garuda Toolbox was started with --boot-repair. Nothing is written to a disk the running system uses.

repair-failed.string: The disks could not be read

repair-failed-detail.string: The log says why. Use Refresh to try once more.

repair-missing.string: Boot repair cannot work on this system

repair-missing-detail.string: These programs are missing: {tools}. Install them and use Refresh.

repair-none-detail.string: No disk holds a partition with a Linux file system or an encrypted partition.

repair-hidden.string: Boot repair is only offered on the live system

repair-root-detail.string: The partition that holds the system that does not start. Every partition with a Linux file system and every encrypted one is listed.

repair-uefi-detail.string: The live system was started through UEFI, so the boot loader is installed for UEFI.

repair-bios-detail.string: The live system was started the legacy way, so GRUB is installed into the boot sector of a disk. systemd-boot and any UEFI installation need the live system started through UEFI.

repair-locked-detail.string: You are asked for the passphrase before a repair. The partition is locked again afterwards.

repair-layout-detail.string: Garuda installs into the subvolume @, a Btrfs folder that holds the system. Choose the top of the file system only for a system that was installed without subvolumes.

repair-layout-subvolume.string: In the subvolume @ (Garuda's layout, a Btrfs folder that holds the system)

repair-layout-plain.string: At the top of the file system

repair-layout-subvolume-short.developer_comment: The same, short enough for the choice on the page.

repair-layout-plain-short.string: At the top of the file system

repair-in-use.string: The running system uses the disk of this partition, so it cannot be repaired from here. Start the live system from another medium, or unmount what is mounted from that disk and use Refresh.

repair-esp-detail.string: The boot loader is written to this partition. A system with systemd-boot also keeps its kernel images there.

repair-target-disk-detail.string: GRUB is written to the first sectors of this disk. Choose the disk the computer starts from.

repair-no-esp.string: No EFI system partition was found on a disk that is free, so no boot loader can be installed. The boot menu of a GRUB system can still be written again.

repair-no-disk.string: No free disk was found, so GRUB cannot be installed.

repair-running.string: The repair is running. The Console shows its output.

repair-succeeded.string: The repair finished without an error. Restart the computer without the live medium to try the installed system.

repair-failed-run.string: The repair failed. Nothing stays mounted or unlocked. The Console shows which command failed.

repair-busy.string: Another task was running, so the repair did not start. Try again when it has finished.

repair-reinstall-title.developer_comment:
The confirm dialog. $system and $target are devices, $disks and $disk
the disks they lie on.

repair-does-regenerate.string: On a GRUB system the boot menu /boot/grub/grub.cfg of the system on {system} (disk {disks}) is written again. Nothing else on the disk changes. A system with systemd-boot is not repaired this way without UEFI.

repair-does-regenerate-uefi.string: On a GRUB system the boot menu /boot/grub/grub.cfg of the system on {system} (disk {disks}) is written again. On a system with systemd-boot its initramfs and kernel images are built again onto the EFI system partition {esp}. Nothing else on the disks changes.

repair-does-uefi.string: The boot loader is written to the EFI system partition {target} on the disk {disk} and entered into the firmware's boot menu: GRUB as "Garuda", systemd-boot as "Linux Boot Manager". Then the boot files of the system on {system} (disk {disks}) are built again: GRUB's boot menu /boot/grub/grub.cfg, or systemd-boot's kernel images.

repair-does-bios.string: GRUB is written to the first sectors of the disk {target}, in place of the boot loader that is there now. Then the boot menu /boot/grub/grub.cfg of the system on {system} (disk {disks}) is written again. A system with systemd-boot is not repaired this way.

repair-looked-for.string: The system is looked for here: {layout}
repair-looked-for.developer_comment: $layout is one of the layouts above.

repair-runs-now.string: It runs right away and asks for an administrator's password. The Console shows every command.

repair-encrypted.string: {system} is encrypted. It is unlocked for the repair and locked again afterwards. The passphrase is not kept in any file of Garuda Toolbox.

repair-refused-not-offered.string: Boot repair is only offered on the live system.

repair-refused-unavailable.string: The disks could not be read, so nothing can be repaired.

repair-refused-unknown-system.string: This system is not in the list anymore. Read the disks again.

repair-refused-in-use.string: The running system uses this disk, so nothing is written to it.

repair-refused-unknown-target.string: Choose where the boot loader goes first.

repair-refused-unknown-layout.string: Choose where the system lies first.

repair-refused-empty.string: Enter the passphrase of the encrypted partition.

repair-refused-control-character.string: The passphrase holds a line break or another character that cannot be typed.

repair-refused-other.string: The repair could not be started.

repair-why-passphrase.string: Enter the passphrase to go on.

catalog-components-pipewire-support-desc.string: The modern standard for handling audio and video streams on Linux. It seamlessly replaces PulseAudio and JACK with much lower latency and better security.

catalog-components-jack-support-descript.string: A specialized, low-latency sound server designed for professional audio production. Usually handled natively by PipeWire now.

catalog-components-pulseaudio-support-de.string: The older, legacy sound server. Kept primarily for compatibility, but PipeWire has largely replaced it.

catalog-components-group-realtime-descri.string: Adds your user to the realtime group, giving audio applications CPU priority to prevent stuttering and latency.

catalog-components-easyeffects-descripti.string: A powerful tool to enhance your microphone quality and audio playback. Highly recommended to install 'Calf Plugins' and 'LSP Plugins' alongside this for a complete experience.

catalog-components-lsp-plugins-descripti.string: Linux Studio Plugins (LSP). A collection of professional audio tools like equalizers and compressors. Install this to expand EasyEffects' capabilities.

catalog-components-calf-description.string: Calf Studio Gear. A high-quality set of audio processing plugins. Install this to give EasyEffects more professional studio effects.

catalog-components-jamesdsp-description.string: An audio effect processor for adding bass boost, equalizers, and other effects. It is recommended to try EasyEffects first.

catalog-components-virt-manager-descript.string: A powerful desktop application (GUI) for creating and managing KVM/QEMU virtual machines.

catalog-components-enabled-libvirtd-desc.string: The system daemon required to run and manage virtual machines and other virtualization platforms.

catalog-components-group-libvirt-descrip.string: Adds your user to the libvirt group, granting permission to manage advanced KVM/QEMU virtual machines.

catalog-components-group-kvm-description.string: Adds your user to the kvm group, granting permission to use fast, hardware-accelerated KVM virtual machines.

catalog-components-qemu-description.string: A generic, open-source machine emulator and virtualizer. Can run operating systems for any machine, on any machine.

catalog-components-virtualbox-descriptio.string: Oracle's popular cross-platform virtualization software. Very user-friendly, though generally slower than KVM/Virt-Manager.

catalog-components-group-vboxusers-descr.string: Adds your user to the vboxusers group, granting permission to use VirtualBox.

catalog-components-qemu-user-static-desc.string: Can be used to Run foreign architecture binaries natively, i.e. via Podman

catalog-components-qemu-user-static-binf.string: Register foreign arch handlers in kernel, this can be useful when attempting to run aarch64 container images.

catalog-components-docker-description.string: The industry-standard container engine for packaging and running isolated applications.

catalog-components-enabled-docker-descri.string: Runs the background daemon required to manage and run Docker containers.

catalog-components-group-docker-descript.string: Adds your user to the docker group, granting permission to run Docker commands without sudo.

catalog-components-docker-compose-descri.string: A tool for defining and running multi-container Docker applications via configuration files.

catalog-components-podman-description.string: A modern, daemonless alternative to Docker. It runs containers without needing root privileges, offering better security.

catalog-components-podman-desktop-descri.string: A graphical application to easily manage, create, and view your Podman containers.

catalog-components-podman-docker-descrip.string: A compatibility package that aliases the 'docker' command to 'podman', so existing Docker scripts work seamlessly with Podman.

catalog-components-distrobox-description.string: Creates tightly integrated containers of other Linux distributions. Lets you install and run apps from Ubuntu, Fedora, or Arch natively inside Garuda.

catalog-components-kontainer-description.string: A native KDE application for managing Distrobox containers with ease.

catalog-components-boxbuddy-description.string: A graphical app to easily manage and use your Distrobox environments.

catalog-components-winboat-description.string: Uses containerization to provide seamlessly integrated Windows apps on Linux.

catalog-components-networkmanager-descri.string: The core daemon that configures and manages your Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and VPN connections.

catalog-components-enabled-networkmanage.string: Runs the NetworkManager daemon so you can connect to the internet.

catalog-components-enabled-modemmanager-.string: Runs the daemon required to connect to the internet using mobile broadband (4G/5G USB modems).

catalog-components-bluetooth-support-des.string: The BlueZ Linux Bluetooth stack. Provides the core software needed to handle wireless devices.

catalog-components-enabled-bluetooth-des.string: Runs the background service required to pair and connect to Bluetooth devices.

catalog-components-autoconnect-descripti.string: Automatically reconnects to your trusted, previously paired Bluetooth devices when they power on.

catalog-components-autoconnect-enabled-d.string: Runs the background service that actively handles automatic Bluetooth reconnections.

catalog-components-printing-support-desc.string: CUPS (Common Unix Printing System). The core software needed to connect and print to local or network printers.

catalog-components-scanning-support-desc.string: SANE (Scanner Access Now Easy). The core software needed to use flatbed and document scanners.

catalog-components-enabled-cups-descript.string: Runs the CUPS daemon required to handle print jobs and manage printers.

catalog-components-enabled-saned-descrip.string: Runs the daemon that allows you to share your scanner over the local network.

catalog-components-group-cups-descriptio.string: Adds your user to the cups group, granting permission to manage printers and print queues.

catalog-components-group-scanner-descrip.string: Adds your user to the scanner group, granting permission to use document scanners.

catalog-components-group-lp-description.string: Adds your user to the lp (line printer) group, required by some older printing systems.

catalog-components-ufw-description.string: Uncomplicated Firewall. A simpler command-line interface for managing iptables/nftables firewall rules.

catalog-components-enabled-ufw-descripti.string: Runs the UFW service to enforce your simple firewall rules.

catalog-components-firewalld-description.string: A dynamic firewall manager that uses zones to dynamically define network trust levels and rules.

catalog-components-enabled-firewalld-des.string: Runs the firewalld daemon to protect your system from incoming network connections.

catalog-components-opensnitch-descriptio.string: An application-level firewall that alerts you and asks for permission whenever a program tries to connect to the internet.

catalog-components-enabled-opensnitch-de.string: Runs the OpenSnitch daemon to monitor application network traffic.

catalog-components-gns-description.string: Integrates the Nix package manager, giving you access to thousands of extra software packages. Also provides a NixOS installation sharing settings with Garuda.

catalog-settings-profile-sync-daemon-des.string: Moves your web browser's profile (like Firefox or Brave) into fast temporary RAM (tmpfs). This significantly speeds up browser responsiveness and reduces wear on your SSD.

catalog-settings-enable-profile-sync-dae.string: Runs the Profile-sync-daemon to automatically manage your browser profiles in RAM.

catalog-settings-systemd-oomd-descriptio.string: systemd's Out-Of-Memory daemon. It actively monitors system memory and automatically terminates memory-hogging processes before your entire computer freezes up.

catalog-settings-guest-user-description.string: Creates a temporary 'guest' user account with no password, isolated from your personal files. Wiped on logout.

catalog-settings-performance-tweaks-desc.string: Applies a set of system-level sysctl and tuning configurations to optimize Garuda for maximum responsiveness.

catalog-settings-ananicy-cpp-description.string: Auto NICe daemon. Dynamically changes the CPU priority (niceness) of running processes, giving the active application you are currently using more CPU time so the system feels faster.

catalog-settings-enable-ananicy-cpp-desc.string: Runs the Ananicy daemon to continuously manage application CPU priorities.

catalog-settings-bpftune-git-description.string: Uses eBPF to continuously monitor and automatically tune your Linux network parameters in real-time for optimal internet throughput and latency.

catalog-settings-enable-bpftune-descript.string: Runs the bpftune daemon to continuously optimize your network performance.

catalog-settings-enabled-preload-descrip.string: Runs the Preload daemon to cache your frequently used applications.

catalog-settings-enabled-irqbalance-desc.string: Distributes hardware interrupts evenly across all your CPU cores. This prevents a single core from getting bogged down handling device signals.

catalog-settings-powersave-tweaks-descri.string: Applies sysctl and configuration tweaks designed to minimize power consumption on battery-operated devices.

catalog-settings-thermald-description.string: Intel's thermal management daemon. It prevents your system from overheating by proactively using cooling methods before forcing the CPU to throttle down.

catalog-settings-enabled-thermald-descri.string: Runs the thermald daemon to monitor CPU temperatures and prevent overheating.

catalog-settings-power-profiles-daemon-d.string: Provides an API for the system to easily switch between 'Power Saver', 'Balanced', and 'Performance' operating modes.

catalog-settings-enabled-power-profiles-.string: Runs the daemon that allows your desktop environment to toggle power profiles.

catalog-settings-intel-undervolt-descrip.string: Lowers the voltage supplied to Intel processors. This reduces heat and power consumption without sacrificing performance, which extends battery life and prevents thermal throttling.

catalog-settings-enabled-intel-undervolt.string: Runs the daemon that automatically applies your Intel undervolt settings on boot.

catalog-settings-rightclick-emulation-pa.string: Configures libinput so that holding a single finger on a touchscreen or touchpad registers as a right-click.

catalog-settings-audio-no-suspend-descri.string: Disables PipeWire's node-suspend feature. This keeps audio devices constantly active, preventing the annoying popping or clicking noises that occur when sound cards wake up from sleep.

catalog-settings-kde-borderless-maximize.string: A KWin tweak that removes the title bar and window borders when an application is maximized in KDE Plasma, giving you more usable vertical screen space.

catalog-settings-discord-disable-autoupd.string: Prevents Discord from prompting to download and installing updates, since this is totally useless on Archlinux - Pacman does it for us.

catalog-gaming-bottles-description.string: Easily manage wine and proton prefix

catalog-gaming-heroic-games-launcher-bin.string: An Open source Launcher for Epic, Amazon and GOG Games

catalog-gaming-itch-setup-bin-descriptio.string: Installer for the itch.io desktop app

catalog-gaming-mangohud-description.string: A Vulkan overlay layer for monitoring FPS, temperatures, CPU/GPU load and more

catalog-gaming-steamtinkerlaunch-descrip.string: Wrapper script for Steam custom launch options

catalog-gaming-vkbasalt-description.string: A Vulkan post-processing layer. Some of the effects are CAS, FXAA, SMAA, deband

catalog-gaming-discord-description.string: All-in-one voice and text chat for gamers

catalog-gaming-vesktop-description.string: Vesktop is a customizable and privacy friendly Discord desktop app

catalog-gaming-gameconqueror-description.string: Memory scanner designed to isolate the address of an arbitrary variable in an executing process

catalog-gaming-input-remapper-git-descri.string: A tool to change and program the mapping of your input device buttons

catalog-gaming-keyboard-visualizer-git-d.string: Turn your OpenRGB-supported RGB setup into a spectacular light show for your music

maintenance-op-remove-orphans-detail.string: Remove packages that were installed as dependencies and are no longer needed.

share-delete-detail.string: Nobody can open the link afterwards, you included. Your browser opens the delete link.

share-upload-network.string: The upload failed. bin.garudalinux.org could not be reached. Check the network connection.

report.string: The upload failed. The paste service refused the report, for example because it is too large.

output.string: The upload failed. The paste service refused the output, for example because it is too large.

command-apply-tooltip.string: Run every queued change now, with one password

command-toggle-sidebar-tooltip.string: Show or hide the page names in the sidebar

command-toggle-console-tooltip.string: Show or hide the console with the output of the last run

command-open-palette-tooltip.string: Find a page, a command or an app by its name

command-review-changes-tooltip.string: List the queued changes before you apply them

command-clear-changes-tooltip.string: Remove every queued change. This cannot be undone

command-quit-tooltip.string: Close Garuda Toolbox. Queued changes are kept

command-focus-search-tooltip.string: Put the cursor into the search of the open page

command-help-tooltip.string: Open the user guide on the page about the open one

toast-name.developer_comment: Notes at the top right of the page about background results.

toast-plan-failed.string: A step failed. Open the Console to see what happened.

settings-not-saved.string: A setting could not be saved.

toast-queue-not-saved.string: The queued changes could not be saved. They are lost when the app closes.

toast-queue-edited-outside.string: The queue was changed from the command line.
toast-queue-edited-outside.developer_comment: A garuda-toolbox queue command changed the window's queued changes.

toast-tool-failed.string: {name} ended with an error. The log file says why.
toast-tool-failed.developer_comment:
A program the app started, such as the installer or a Maintenance tool,
ended with an error. $name is its program name.

toast-copied.developer_comment: After Copy name in a row menu.

pane-sidebar.developer_comment: The names of the window's parts for screen readers.

status-probes-failed.string: Some parts of the system could not be read: {parts}
status-probes-failed.developer_comment: $parts lists the parts by their names below, joined by commas.

toggles-all.developer_comment: The chip that shows every section.

toggles-nothing-matches-detail.string: No entry of this page has “{search}” in its name or description.

toggles-section-count.developer_comment: $on and $total are counts of the entries of a section, a chip or the page, shown as "2/8".

toggles-unknown.string: {count, plural, one {The state of one entry could not be read, so its switch may show the wrong state.} other {The state of {count} entries could not be read, so their switches may show the wrong state.}}

toggles-needs.developer_comment: $names lists the titles of the entries, joined by commas.

toggles-problem.string: The list could not be loaded.
toggles-problem.developer_comment: Why the catalog could not be loaded.

toggles-problem-unreadable.string: A catalog file could not be read.

toggles-problem-invalid.string: An entry of a catalog file breaks a rule.

tweaks-shell-description.string: It is recommended to use a POSIX-compliant shell such as Bash or Zsh, and Fish only through your terminal's profile.

tweaks-dns-description.string: The servers that look up the addresses of websites for this computer.

tweaks-wifi-description.string: iwd is a lighter alternative to wpa_supplicant. It often connects faster and handles roaming better.

tweaks-hblock-description.string: Block ads, trackers and malware domains with hblock.

tweaks-flag-skip-mirrorlist-description.string: Skip choosing the fastest Arch download servers (the mirrorlist) before running system updates.

tweaks-flag-update-aur-description.string: Update packages installed from the Arch User Repository (AUR) during system updates.

tweaks-flag-pacman-noconfirm-description.string: Run pacman, the package manager, without asking you to confirm, for a faster update. It then takes its default answer to every question.

tweaks-flag-no-check-space-description.string: Skip checking available disk space before installing packages.

page-users-subtitle.string: Add users, set passwords, lock accounts and change groups.

users-search-detail.string: The search looks at user names, user IDs, full names, home folders, shells and groups.

users-regular-only-detail.string: Hides the accounts of the system and its services.

users-count.developer_comment: $shown is how many the filter and search let through, $count all accounts.

users-none-regular-detail.string: Clear the filter to see the accounts of the system.

users-keys.string: Arrow keys pick an account. Return edits it, the Menu key opens its other actions.

users-tag-queued.string: {count, plural, one {1 change queued} other {{count} changes queued}}

users-edit-named.developer_comment: What a screen reader hears for the row button above. $user is the account.

users-root.string: Root accounts are not changed here.

users-locks-dismissed.string: Which accounts are locked is not known: the password dialog was closed.

users-locks-denied.string: Which accounts are locked is not known: the password dialog was closed or the password was not accepted.

users-locks-no-agent.string: Which accounts are locked is not known: no password dialog could appear, because this desktop session runs no polkit authentication agent (the program that asks for your password when an app needs more rights).

users-locks-helper-missing.string: Which accounts are locked is not known: the helper of Garuda Toolbox is not installed. Reinstall Garuda Toolbox.

users-locks-unknown.string: Which accounts are locked is not known: the helper of Garuda Toolbox could not read it.

users-run-password-failed.string: The password of {user} could not be set. The Console shows why.

users-run-new-account-failed.string: The account {user} could not be added. The Console shows why.

users-refused-root.string: {name} is a root account. Garuda Toolbox does not change it.

users-refused-current-user.string: {name} is the account you are logged in with. It cannot lock or remove itself.

users-refused-system-account.string: {name} is a system account. Only accounts of people can be removed.

users-refused-outside-user-range.string: {name} has a user ID outside 1000 to 60000, so it stays as it is.

users-refused-last-admin.string: {name} is the last member of the groups wheel and sudo. Without one nobody could administer this system.

users-refused-last-admin-lock.string: {name} is the last member of the groups wheel and sudo. With a locked password nobody could administer this system.

users-refused-lock-state-unknown.string: {name} cannot be locked while it is unknown which admins are locked.

users-refused-primary-group.string: {name} is the primary group of a user, so it stays.

users-refused-system-group.string: {name} is a system group. Installed programs rely on it.

users-refused-unknown-group.string: One of the groups does not exist, or is about to be removed.

users-refused-shell-not-listed.string: This shell is not listed in /etc/shells.

users-refused-uid-invalid.string: The user ID is a whole number from 1 to 60000.

users-refused-uid-in-use.string: Another account already has this user ID.

users-refused-uid-out-of-range.string: Accounts of people take a user ID from 1000 to 60000, system accounts one below 1000.

users-refused-home-taken.string: Another account already has this home folder.

users-refused-unavailable.string: The user accounts of this system could not be read.

users-name-invalid-start.string: Names start with a lowercase letter or an underscore.

users-name-invalid-character.string: Only lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores are allowed.

users-home-too-long.string: The home folder is too long.

users-home-not-absolute.string: The home folder is a full path that starts with a slash, such as /home/ada.

users-home-invalid-character.string: The home folder cannot hold a colon, a line break or another control character.

users-home-outer-blank.string: The home folder cannot start or end with a blank.

users-home-invalid-component.string: The home folder cannot hold “..”, a single dot, two slashes in a row or a slash at the end.

users-home-outside-roots.string: The home folder must lie below /home, /srv, /var/lib or /opt.

users-full-name-too-long.string: The full name is too long.

users-full-name-invalid-character.string: The full name cannot hold a colon, comma, equals sign, quotation mark or line break.

users-full-name-leading-dash.string: The full name cannot start with a hyphen.

users-full-name-outer-blank.string: The full name cannot start or end with a blank.

users-password-control-character.string: The password cannot hold a line break or another control character.

users-field-name-hint.string: Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, at most 32 characters.

users-field-shell-hint.string: Only shells listed in /etc/shells can be chosen.

users-field-home-hint.string: Optional. A full path. Leave it empty for the usual folder below /home.

users-field-uid-hint.string: Optional. 1000 to 60000 for a person, below 1000 for a system account.

users-no-home-detail.string: The account gets no folder of its own.

users-system-detail.string: For a service, not a person: a user ID below 1000, hidden by “Regular users only”.

users-admin-detail.string: May install software and change the system, after entering their own password. This puts the user into the group {group}.

users-other-groups.string: Other groups beside the user's own one

users-add-note.string: The user is created right away. This asks for your own password.

users-add-why-no-name.developer_comment: Beside the greyed out "Add user now": the first thing it waits for.

users-add-why-bad-name.string: The user name cannot be used. The note under it says why.

users-add-why-fields.string: A field above says what is wrong.

users-add-why-busy.string: Waits until the changes being applied are done.

users-move-files.string: Move the files to the new folder

users-move-yes.string: Applying this moves every file from {old} to {new}. The new folder must not exist yet, and {user} must be logged out. On another disk this copies everything and can take long.

users-move-no.string: Only the entry of the account changes and no file is moved: everything stays in {old}. {new} must exist already, or {user} has no home folder at the next login. {user} must be logged out when you apply this.

users-home-current-user.string: The home folder of the account you are logged in with cannot change while it runs programs.

users-edit-note.string: The changes wait in the queue until you apply them.

users-password-note.string: The password is set right away and asks for your own password. This page shows when it is done. The password is not kept in the queue or in any file of Garuda Toolbox.

users-groups-note.string: Changes wait in the queue until you apply them. They take effect at the user's next login.

users-remove-goes.string: The removal waits in the queue until you apply it. This goes:

users-remove-group.string: The group {user}, when the user is its only member

users-remove-home-goes.string: The home folder {home} with every file in it, and the mail spool

users-remove-home-stays.string: The home folder {home} stays on the disk.

groups-search-detail.string: The search looks at group names, group IDs and members.

groups-remove-detail.string: Its members leave it. Files that belong to the group keep its number as their group. The removal waits in the queue until you apply it.

groups-add-note.string: The group waits in the queue until you apply it. Users can be put into it before that.
